passage: Payal, you asked how I felt when Meenu and I went for the same promotion. Come, I will tell you. I was twenty-six, and we sat two desks apart. I counted every compliment she got. Once I saw her draft lying on the printer, and for a wicked minute I stood there with my hand out, thinking of hiding it. Then I heard my own breath and stepped back. That night I went to my desk and reworked my own client proposal. When the result came, Meenu got the role. I congratulated her, and it cost me. But in the next year I did the best work of my life, and Meenu and I became friends. Rivalry can sharpen you, Payal, if it does not rot you. Indu

qa.q: How old was Indu when competing with Meenu for the promotion?
Why did Indu step back from the printer?
qa.a: Indu caught the impulse and recognised that hiding the draft would betray honest work and Indu's character.

qa.q: What did Indu do to compete honestly?
qa.a: Reworked Indu's own client proposal that night and focused on visible results.

qa.q: How might Meenu have seen Indu's congratulations?
qa.a: Meenu likely received it as a gracious gesture, and their later friendship suggests it was welcomed.

grounding: An elder recalls competing for a promotion, resisting sabotage, focusing on work and staying honest.

passage: "Honestly? When Farida and I were both shortlisted for team lead, I became someone I didn't like. I'm Elizabeth, by the way, I run freight bookings for a logistics firm in Leeds. I started counting her emails. I noticed when she left early. One night I caught myself drafting a message to our director about a small mistake of hers, a typo in a supplier sheet, and I just stopped, hand on the mouse. That wasn't about work. So I deleted it and did the boring thing instead. I fixed our delayed-shipments dashboard, wrote up the results, sent them round. When Farida asked for help with the audit, I helped. She got the role, actually. It stung for a week. But I'd still rather be the one who stopped drafting that email."

qa.q: Who else was shortlisted for team lead with Elizabeth?
What was Elizabeth feeling when she stopped with a hand on the mouse?
qa.a: She felt uneasy and ashamed of the rivalry, seeing that the message about a typo came from tension, not from concern for the work.

qa.q: What did Elizabeth do instead of sending the message?
qa.a: She deleted it, fixed the delayed-shipments dashboard, wrote up the results, and helped Farida with the audit.

qa.q: How might Farida have seen Elizabeth during the shortlist?
qa.a: Farida probably saw a tense but fair rival, and was likely grateful that Elizabeth helped with the audit rather than working against her.

grounding: Two colleagues compete for a promotion; the protagonist feels calculating but chooses honest, visible work over sabotage.

passage:
Monday: The partners announced one project-lead post, and Pradeep felt his jaw tighten when Dolma's model got a nod. That evening he stayed late, listing her weak points on a sticky note.
Thursday: Dolma's site file vanished from the shared drive, and she went pale in front of everyone. Pradeep knew she had saved a copy on his machine last month. For a second, he said nothing. Then he opened the folder. "It's here," he called. Dolma exhaled and mouthed thanks.
Two weeks later: Pradeep presented his school-library design with measurements he had checked three times. It was the sharpest work he had done all year. The sticky note had gone into the bin. Whoever got the post, he could look at his drawings, and at Dolma, without flinching.

qa.q: Where was the copy of Dolma's site file?
qa.a: On Pradeep's machine, where she had saved it last month.

qa.q: Why did Pradeep hesitate before speaking on Thursday?
qa.a: He was tempted to let his rival struggle; the tension of competing made silence feel useful for a second before his honesty won.

qa.q: What changed in how Pradeep competed by the third beat?
qa.a: He threw away the list of Dolma's weak points and put his energy into careful, visible work on his own design.

qa.q: What is it like for Dolma when her file goes missing?
qa.a: She is anxious and exposed in front of everyone, then relieved when Pradeep finds the copy, and likely sees him as a fair rival after that.

grounding: A protagonist competing for a promotion feels tense and tempted but stays honest and lets the rivalry sharpen his own work.
